B: '104.2% of expected row floor' and 'case-insensitive substring' are not in the shown reference record.

The verdict range of 5,500-9,000 contradicts its own scenario table.

raw.verdict: B and D both reproduced the measured rise to the 2022 peak and the decline to 776, along with the flat no-change projection and its widening bounds. B went further: it charted the central scenario, exported the scenario rows, and used a pre-pandemic baseline. It also explained why naive linear extrapolation fails (worse MAE, and no-change over-predicting a falling series), which is exactly the trap this question sets. A honestly declined to answer, while C offered memory estimates on a different scale with an internally inconsistent range.
